x2_self_referential_numbers_for_comparis.note: FIG_constraint_count_vs_completion_x2.png. There the target trajectory AND the yardstick were the model's OWN dense decode (projected onto X2's limits), so the experiment could only measure 'can sparse conditioning recover what dense conditioning gave'. The constraint SETS 1..5 are identical to the ones used here, so the columns line up exactly. X2 additionally had a 6th set (+head) that reached 0.243 cm; there is no 6th set here.
x2_self_referential_numbers_for_comparis.verdict: The monotone improvement SURVIVES the switch to an external reference. At matched constraint counts the GT-referenced G1 numbers are as good as or better than the self-referential X2 ones. The caveat that the X2 run never tested is the IK-only-from-rest control reported here: much of the gain is geometric, not model-driven.

controls_added_here_that_the_x2_run_did_.IK_only_from_rest: the identical pin, identical targets, warm-started from the bare rest pose instead of the model's decode — what pure IK gets with no model at all
controls_added_here_that_the_x2_run_did_.offchain_joints: completion restricted to joints that are neither commanded nor an ancestor of a commanded joint, i.e. the ones no command reaches; at 5 commands only 5 of 36 G1 joints qualify
